speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are experiencing fatigue, abdominal pain, night sweats, and weight loss, along with an enlarged supraclavicular lymph node. To help narrow down the cause, can you tell me if you have had any changes in your bowel habits, such as diarrhea or constipation, recently?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for confirming those symptoms. To help pinpoint the source of the abdominal pain and lymph node involvement, have you noticed any specific location of the pain, such as the upper right or lower left quadrant, and have you experienced any recent fever?

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Doctor
text: A fixed, non-tender supraclavicular lymph node is highly concerning for malignancy, particularly gastrointestinal or thoracic cancer. To help differentiate between potential causes, have you experienced any persistent cough, shortness of breath, or difficulty swallowing recently?

speaker: Patient
text: I also feel fullness in my abdomen and my clothes feel tighter. I do not have cough or recent travel.

speaker: Doctor
text: The abdominal fullness and early satiety suggest possible gastric involvement or ascites, which, combined with the supraclavicular node, raises suspicion for gastric cancer. To evaluate for anemia and systemic inflammation, I will order some blood work and imaging. REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count, REQUEST TEST: CT_Abdomen_Pelvis

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete_Blood_Count: WBC Elevated, Hemoglobin Slightly Decreased, Platelets Normal. CT_Abdomen_Pelvis: Slight abdominal distension, Dullness noted over the left lower quadrant, Splenomegaly detected.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of splenomegaly shifts the differential toward a hematologic malignancy like lymphoma rather than solid tumor metastasis. I need to confirm the nature of the lymph node involvement. REQUEST TEST: Lymph_Node_Biopsy

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Cervical_Lymph_Node_Biopsy: Lymphocytes with a high proliferative index that stain positive for CD20.

speaker: Doctor
text: The biopsy results showing CD20-positive lymphocytes with a high proliferative index are diagnostic of a B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma, likely diffuse large B-cell lymphoma given the aggressive symptoms. DIAGNOSIS READY: Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma
